  "extractions": [
    {
      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],
        "scope_text": "For an employee of a covered employer seeking status as an eligible employee under FMLA.",
        "context_quotes": ["F003", "F004"],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F002", "F003", "F004"],
        "choice_quote": "F001:F004",
        "choice_text": "All three requirements must be satisfied: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special rules in § 825.801); AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.",
        "logic_quote": "F001:F004",
        "references": ["§ 825.801", "§ 825.105(b)"],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) regarding employees working outside the U.S.)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005"],
        "scope_text": "In meeting the requirement that an employee must have been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": ["F006", "F007:F009"],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F005",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the applicable break in service rules are met."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005", "F006"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.",
        "context_quotes": ["F007:F009"],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F006",
        "references": ["paragraph (b)(2)"],
        "statement": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F007"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where an employee has experienced a break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F008", "F009"],
        "choice_quote": "F007:F009",
        "choice_text": "Either: (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "logic_quote": "F007:F009",
        "references": ["USERRA", "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where: (i) the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of the employee's USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F008",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F007", "F008"],
        "scope_text": "Where an employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation, in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F008",
        "references": ["USERRA", "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."],
        "statement": "The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under USERRA."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F010"],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (such as workers' compensation or group health plan benefits), the week counts as a week of employment, and for intermittent, occasional, or casual employment, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F011"],
        "scope_text": "When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "Nothing in this section prevents",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Employers may consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F011"],
        "scope_text": "If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment preceding a continuous break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F012"],
        "scope_text": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, in determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": ["paragraph (c)(2)", "§ 825.801", "FLSA", "29 CFR part 785"],
        "statement": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to FLSA principles for compensable hours of work based on the actual hours worked for the employer, without limitation by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F012"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": ["FLSA"],
        "statement": "Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F013"],
        "scope_text": "For an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service, in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave.",
        "context_quotes": ["F013"],
        "modality_quote": "shall",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": ["USERRA", "§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service must be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, adding those hours to actual hours worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F013"],
        "scope_text": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "can generally",
        "modality": "possible",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": ["USERRA", "§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "The employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations to determine the hours that would have been worked during the absence due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service (noting special rules in § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F014"],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "has the burden of showing",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": ["FLSA Regulations, 29 CFR part 541", "§ 825.102", "§ 825.801(d)"],
        "statement": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including FLSA-exempt employees), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim ineligibility."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F015"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": ["F015"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": ["§ 825.300(b)"],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F015"],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "would be",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": ["§ 825.300(b)"],
        "statement": "An employee may be on non-FMLA leave when meeting the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement is FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "To ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits regarding whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "is determined when",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave, and once determined eligible in response to that notice, eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in employee count within 75 miles for that specific notice, whether leave is taken all at once, intermittently, or on a reduced schedule."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "prohibition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "When employee leave has already started and the employee count within 75 miles subsequently drops below 50.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may not",
        "modality": "must_not",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employer must not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "When an employer employs 50 or more employees (e.g., 60 employees in August) at the time an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave, even if the employer expects the count to drop below 50 (e.g., to 40 in December) by the time leave begins.",
        "context_quotes": [],

        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",

        "statement": "An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave when the employer meets the 50-employee threshold, even if the number of employees is expected to drop below 50 by the time the leave begins."
      }
    }
  ]

unit_attributes.scope_text: For an employee of a covered employer seeking status as an eligible employee under FMLA.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three requirements must be satisfied: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special rules in § 825.801); AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) regarding employees working outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In meeting the requirement that an employee must have been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the applicable break in service rules are met.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where an employee has experienced a break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either: (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where: (i) the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of the employee's USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Where an employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation, in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (such as workers' compensation or group health plan benefits), the week counts as a week of employment, and for intermittent, occasional, or casual employment, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Employers may consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment preceding a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, in determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to FLSA principles for compensable hours of work based on the actual hours worked for the employer, without limitation by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service, in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service must be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, adding those hours to actual hours worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations to determine the hours that would have been worked during the absence due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service (noting special rules in § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including FLSA-exempt employees), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim ineligibility.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave when meeting the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement is FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: To ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits regarding whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave, and once determined eligible in response to that notice, eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in employee count within 75 miles for that specific notice, whether leave is taken all at once, intermittently, or on a reduced schedule.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When employee leave has already started and the employee count within 75 miles subsequently drops below 50.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employer employs 50 or more employees (e.g., 60 employees in August) at the time an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave, even if the employer expects the count to drop below 50 (e.g., to 40 in December) by the time leave begins.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave when the employer meets the 50-employee threshold, even if the number of employees is expected to drop below 50 by the time the leave begins.
